subject: Differential equations and forcing functions using data?

messages.author: 4b681bcd9d4d425d
messages.subject: Differential equations and forcing functions using data?
parts:
Hi all,

I'm working on a differential equation model that STAN can (successfully) solve in a simplified using the integrate_ode function. This works, modulo some problems with convergence, presumably because I'm not capturing the underlying dynamics correctly.

In order to capture those underlying dynamics, I need to have some of my parameters use a forcing model - but i can't figure out how to do this, given that the forcing function is based on data, and so it is not parametric in t. (It doesn't help that I never took that ODE class in undergrad, and scrambled to learn different parts on their own, so I'm probably missing something basic.)

Does anyone have any advice / examples of having done this? Or is there some reason it's not possible?

Thanks,
David Manheim

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Differential equations and forcing functions using data?
parts:
More details would be better, but I can confirm you that forcings work in Stan. I.e. I have run an analysis where I model the response to a drug while using the drug concentration over time as (fixed) input function. The difficult part is to code this in Stan, but what it takes is to make use of the x_r and x_i (fixed data) portion of the integrate_ode function. You have to figure out what data you have to pass into the function in order to be able to calculate at any time-point t the values of the forcing function entering your differential.

Sebastian
